mainTopic: The כתובה of a מוכת עץ and of a woman found not to be a בתולה: רב and שמואל, רבי מאיר and the רבנן, and רבא's retraction
overview: The amud finishes the משנה about women who come into marriage already presumed to be non-virgins. These women get a כתובה of a מנה, and their husband has no טענת בתולים against them. The גמרא then brings a dispute between רב and שמואל about a minor boy who has relations with an adult woman. רב says this makes her a מוכת עץ, and שמואל says there is no מוכת עץ through flesh. Answering רב אושעיא's challenge, רבא shows that the case of מוכת עץ is itself a dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן. רמי בר חמא and then רבא try to explain when a מוכת עץ gets 200, a מנה, or nothing, depending on whether the husband knew about her. Along the way, רב ששת rules that a woman found to be a בעולה gets a מנה, and רב נחמן objects that a מקח טעות means she gets nothing. רבא agrees with רב נחמן and rereads a ברייתא so that a מוכת עץ gets a מנה. From that reading the גמרא concludes that רבא retracted his earlier ruling. The amud ends with a new ברייתא: once a first husband brought a woman in for marriage, a second husband cannot make a טענת בתולים.

steps.title: End of the previous clause: no virginity claim
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the משנה's earlier clause: these women cannot be subject to a טענת בתולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they are not subject to a claim about their virginity.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle. This line finishes the earlier case about a widow, divorcee, or חלוצה who was already married: the new husband cannot complain that she was not a virgin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These women were married before, so everyone assumes they are not virgins. A husband who marries them knowingly cannot later claim he was fooled. That is why there is no טענת בתולים.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's claim that his bride was not a virgin as expected
They do not have, meaning this does not apply to them

phrases.english: And they are not subject to a claim about their virginity.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the women in the משנה's previous line: a widow, a divorcee, or a חלוצה after a full marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a clause of the משנה that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women already presumed non-virgins cannot be subject to a טענת בתולים.

steps.title: Convert, captive, and maidservant over three years old
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that a convert, a ransomed captive, or a freed maidservant who was older than three years and a day gets a כתובה of a מנה and is not subject to a טענת בתולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A convert, a captive, or a maidservant who was ransomed, converted, or freed when she was older than three years and one day: her כתובה is a מנה, and she is not subject to a claim about her virginity.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three more women whose כתובה is only a מנה (100 זוז). The reason is the past each one had before she became a free Jewish woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these women came out of a situation where people assume she may have had relations: as a non-Jew, as a captive, or as a slave. Age three and a day is the cutoff because before that age, virginity is not considered lost. Above it, she enters marriage with the presumed status of a non-virgin, so the husband cannot later complain.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who converted to Judaism
A woman taken captive
A non-Jewish maidservant
Three years and one day, the age above which virginity can be considered lost
100 זוז, the smaller כתובה amount, half the 200 a virgin receives

steps.confusionAlert: Read the three verbs in order with the three women: the captive was ransomed, the convert converted, and the maidservant was freed. They do not all apply to each woman.
steps.whatToRemember: A woman who comes into marriage already presumed to be a non-virgin gets a מנה, and her husband has no טענת בתולים against her.

phrases.english: A female convert, a captive woman, or a maidservant
who were ransomed, who converted, or who were freed,
phrases.notes: The verbs go in a crisscross order: the captive was ransomed, the convert converted, the maidservant was freed.

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵירוֹת עַל בְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: when they were more than three years and one day old,
their marriage contract is one hundred,
and they are not subject to a claim about their virginity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more women to the same category of a מנה with no טענת בתולים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A convert, captive, or maidservant who became free after age three and a day gets a כתובה of a מנה and is not subject to a טענת בתולים.

steps.title: רב: a minor's relations make her a מוכת עץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב יהודה quoting רב: when a minor boy has relations with an adult woman, she gets the status of a מוכת עץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רב said: a minor boy who had relations with an adult woman makes her like a woman whose virginity was ruptured by wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new ruling from רב. When a boy too young for his relations to count has relations with an adult woman, she is treated as if her virginity was lost through an injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוכת עץ lost her virginity through an object, not through relations, so she is not considered a woman who had relations. רב says a minor's relations are not full relations, so the woman falls into this same category of 'damaged, but not through real relations.'

keyTerms.meaning: A minor boy, too young for his relations to count as full relations
Who had relations with
An adult woman
Literally 'struck by wood': a woman whose virginity was lost through an object or injury, not through relations

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A minor boy who had relations with an adult woman —
has made her one ruptured by wood.
phrases.notes: Her status is like a woman whose virginity was lost through an object, because his act does not count as real relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a new ruling connected to the topic of lost virginity and the כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor's relations with an adult woman give her the status of a מוכת עץ.

steps.title: שמואל: there is no מוכת עץ through flesh
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that when he told רב's ruling to שמואל, שמואל rejected it: a human body cannot create the status of מוכת עץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said: there is no 'ruptured by wood' through flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tells us how שמואל reacted to רב's ruling. שמואל disagreed with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל objects to applying the label מוכת עץ here at all. In his view, that category is only for damage done by an object, like wood. Contact between people, even a minor's relations, cannot be put into that category.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in his presence
Flesh, meaning bodily relations, as opposed to an object

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The 'I' is רב יהודה, who is still speaking.

phrases.english: he said: there is no 'ruptured by wood' through flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל rejects the ruling רב יהודה quoted from רב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב's ruling that a minor's relations make the woman a מוכת עץ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The category מוכת עץ does not apply when the cause was flesh, meaning relations.

steps.title: A second version: a direct dispute between רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Some teach this ruling on its own, without רב יהודה's story, as a plain dispute: רב says she becomes a מוכת עץ, and שמואל says there is no מוכת עץ through flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this teaching on its own: a minor boy who had relations with an adult woman. רב said: he makes her one ruptured by wood. And שמואל said: there is no 'ruptured by wood' through flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same teaching. Here it is a simple argument between רב and שמואל, with no report from רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The positions do not change; only the way the teaching was handed down is different. In the first version, שמואל was responding to a ruling told to him. In this version, the two simply hold opposite views on the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (a different version)
A teaching or ruling
On its own, as a separate teaching

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree on the positions: רב says a minor's relations make her a מוכת עץ, and שמואל says there is no מוכת עץ through flesh. They differ only in how the dispute was reported.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it
this teaching on its own:
A minor boy who had relations with an adult woman,
Rav said: he has made her one ruptured by wood,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵין מוּכַּת עֵץ בְּבָשָׂר.
phrases.english: and Shmuel said: there is no 'ruptured by wood' through flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא בְּאַפֵּי נַפְשַׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same dispute in a different form of reporting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב holds that a minor's relations make the woman a מוכת עץ; שמואל holds there is no מוכת עץ through flesh.

steps.title: רב אושעיא challenges רב from a teaching about כתובות
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא quotes a teaching that seems to treat a minor boy's relations differently from a מוכת עץ, which goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא objected: an adult man with a minor girl, a minor boy with an adult woman, and a woman injured by wood all get a כתובה of two hundred, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say a woman injured by wood gets one hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא brings a teaching to attack רב's ruling that a minor boy's relations make a woman a מוכת עץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים only argue about the מוכת עץ case and give her one hundred. That suggests they agree the minor-boy case gets two hundred. If so, a minor boy does NOT make her a מוכת עץ, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: two hundred (זוז), the full כתובה of a בתולה
one hundred (זוז), the smaller כתובה
the Sages, the majority view

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya raised an objection:
An adult man who had relations with a minor girl,
and a minor boy who had relations with an adult woman,
and a woman injured by wood:
their כתובה is two hundred. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the Sages say:
a woman injured by wood, her כתובה is one hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's position from the dispute just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a minor boy's relations make an adult woman a מוכת עץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים lower only the מוכת עץ case to one hundred, which implies the minor-boy case stays at two hundred. So the minor-boy case is not מוכת עץ.

steps.title: רבא rereads the teaching to fit רב
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the teaching's cases are not all equal: the first does nothing, the second creates a מוכת עץ, and only the מוכת עץ is disputed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is what it means. An adult man with a minor girl does nothing, because below this age it is like putting a finger in the eye. A minor boy with an adult woman makes her a מוכת עץ. And the מוכת עץ case itself is the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב אושעיא by explaining the teaching differently, so that it actually supports רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case gets two hundred because nothing lasting happened to the girl. The second case is the same as מוכת עץ, so the Sages' 'one hundred' covers it too. So the teaching fits רב after all.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it means (a rereading of a source)
like putting a finger in the eye: no lasting effect
a dispute

phrases.english: Rava said: this is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: גָּדוֹל הַבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנָּה — וְלֹא כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: an adult man with a minor girl has done nothing,
because below this age,
it is like putting a finger in the eye.
And a minor boy with an adult woman
has made her a מוכת עץ.
And the מוכת עץ case itself
is a dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the cases are not parallel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three cases were listed as separate, equal cases, so the minor boy seemed different from מוכת עץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The minor-boy case is itself מוכת עץ and falls under the dispute, which fits רב.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא limits the dispute to when the husband knew
steps.stepSummary: The dispute about מוכת עץ applies only when the husband knew about her condition. If he did not know, everyone agrees she gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: the dispute is when he knew about her. רבי מאיר compares her to a בוגרת, and the רבנן compare her to a בעולה. But if he did not know, everyone agrees she gets nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא adds a limit on when the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband married her knowing what happened, רבי מאיר says she is like a בוגרת, who still gets two hundred. The רבנן say she is like a בעולה, who gets one hundred. If he did not know, he married her by mistake, so all agree there is no כתובה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: he knew about her condition
a girl past full maturity, who still counts as a בתולה
a woman who has had relations before
everyone agrees

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
The dispute is when he knew about her,
phrases.notes: He means the husband knew before the wedding that she was a מוכת עץ.

phrases.english: for רבי מאיר compares her to a בוגרת,
and the רבנן compare her to a woman who has had relations.
But if he did not know about her,
everyone agrees she gets nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the dispute is about מוכת עץ itself, he defines the case it applies to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only when the husband knew. If he did not know, all agree she gets no כתובה.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי מאיר compare her to a woman who had relations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר compares a מוכת עץ to a בוגרת instead of to a בעולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, why does he compare her to a בוגרת? Let him compare her to a בעולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a question about רבי מאיר's comparison. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her physical sign of being a בתולה is gone, like a בעולה's. So why does רבי מאיר choose the comparison that gives her more?

keyTerms.meaning: why?
compares, likens

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אַמַּאי מְדַמֵּי לַהּ לְבוֹגֶרֶת?
phrases.english: And רבי מאיר, why does he compare her to a בוגרת?
Let him compare her to a woman who has had relations!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אַמַּאי מְדַמֵּי לַהּ לְבוֹגֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי מאיר's comparison from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי מאיר compares her to a בוגרת and not to a בעולה.

steps.title: No person did anything to her
steps.stepSummary: A בעולה had something done to her by a person. A מוכת עץ did not, so she is closer to a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בעולה had an act done to her by a person. This woman did not have an act done to her by a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רבי מאיר compares her to a בוגרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, what counts is whether a person acted on her. Wood is not a person, so she is not like a בעולה.

keyTerms.meaning: an act done by a person

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוּלָה — אִיתְעֲבִיד בַּהּ מַעֲשֶׂה בִּידֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: A woman who has had relations had an act done to her by a person;

phrases.aramaic: הָא — לָא אִיתְעֲבִיד בַּהּ מַעֲשֶׂה בִּידֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: this one had no act done to her by a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוּלָה — אִיתְעֲבִיד בַּהּ מַעֲשֶׂה בִּידֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בעולה was acted on by a person and a מוכת עץ was not, so רבי מאיר compares her to a בוגרת.

steps.title: Why don't the רבנן compare her to a בוגרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the opposite question about the רבנן: why not compare her to a בוגרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, instead of comparing her to a בעולה, let them compare her to a בוגרת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the same question from the other side. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no person acted on her, as just said, why do the רבנן put her together with a בעולה?

keyTerms.meaning: instead of comparing

phrases.english: And the רבנן, instead of comparing her to a woman who has had relations,
let them compare her to a בוגרת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror question to step 9, now about the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן compare her to a בעולה and not to a בוגרת.

steps.title: Something did happen to her
steps.stepSummary: A בוגרת had nothing done to her at all. A מוכת עץ did have something done to her, so she is closer to a בעולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בוגרת had no act done to her at all. This woman had an act done to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the רבנן compare her to a בעולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, any act, even by wood, counts. A בוגרת changed only through growing up naturally, so the מוכת עץ is not like her.

keyTerms.meaning: at all

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the facts. רבי מאיר asks 'did a person act on her?' (no, so she is like a בוגרת and gets two hundred). The רבנן ask 'was any act done to her?' (yes, so she is like a בעולה and gets one hundred).

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹגֶרֶת — לָא אִיתְעֲבִיד בַּהּ מַעֲשֶׂה כְּלָל,
phrases.english: A בוגרת had no act done to her at all;
this one had an act done to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹגֶרֶת — לָא אִיתְעֲבִיד בַּהּ מַעֲשֶׂה כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 and closes the explanation of both sides.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בוגרת had no act at all, while a מוכת עץ did, so the רבנן compare her to a בעולה.

steps.title: רב נחמן challenges the claim that everyone agrees she gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא said that if the husband did not know, all agree she gets nothing. רב נחמן brings a משנה where the husband did not know, and רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר still believe the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he did not know about her condition, everyone agrees she gets nothing. רב נחמן objected: She says, 'I was injured by wood,' and he says, 'No, a man was with you.' רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רמי בר חמא's rule, and then רב נחמן attacks it with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה the husband is clearly surprised, so he did not know about her condition. Even so, רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר believe her, which means she does get a כתובה. So it is not true that everyone agrees she gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He knew about her condition before marrying her
According to everyone; all opinions agree
A woman who was with a man
She is believed

phrases.english: But if he was not aware of her condition —
everyone agrees she gets nothing at all.
Rav Nachman raised an objection:
She says: I was injured by wood,
and he says: Not so,
rather, a man was with you —

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: she is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רמי בר חמא's rule and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's claim that if he did not know, all agree she gets nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה the husband did not know, yet רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר give her a כתובה, so not everyone agrees.

steps.title: רבא explains the dispute a new way
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that for רבי מאיר she gets מאתים whether he knew or not. For the רבנן she gets a מנה if he knew and nothing if he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Whether he knew or did not know, according to רבי מאיר she gets two hundred. According to the רבנן, if he knew she gets a מנה, and if he did not know she gets nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רמי בר חמא's approach and gives a new way to set up the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'he did not know' is no longer something everyone agrees on. רבי מאיר gives her מאתים even then, so the משנה that believes the woman can fit רבי מאיר. Only the רבנן say she gets nothing when he did not know.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this drops the earlier approach
Two hundred זוז, the full כתובה of a בתולה
One hundred זוז, the כתובה of a non-בתולה

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הִכִּיר בָּהּ וּבֵין לֹא הִכִּיר בָּהּ —
phrases.english: Whether he was aware of her condition or not aware of it —
according to Rabbi Meir, two hundred.
According to the Rabbis, if he was aware — one hundred,
if he was not aware — nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge by changing how the dispute is set up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees she gets nothing if he did not know.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the רבנן say nothing; רבי מאיר gives מאתים either way.

steps.title: רבא retracts because of a ברייתא about הוצאת שם רע
steps.stepSummary: רבא took back his view because of a ברייתא. It describes a husband who claims his wife was not a בתולה and says that she gets a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא retracted, because a ברייתא teaches: How does הוצאת שם רע happen? He comes to court and says, 'So-and-so, I did not find your daughter to be a בתולה.' If there are witnesses that she sinned while under him, she gets a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבא changed his mind and brings the ברייתא that made him do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא announces that רבא changed his mind and names this ברייתא as the reason. How it proves the point becomes clear only later. In step 23 רבא reads the ברייתא's מנה case as a מוכת עץ the husband did not know about, which contradicts his earlier ruling (steps 24-25).

keyTerms.meaning: And he retracted; he changed his mind
Spreading a bad name; a husband falsely accusing his wife
Under him; while bound to him

phrases.english: And Rava retracted,
as it was taught in a baraita:
How does slander come about?
He comes to court and says:
So-and-so, I did not find your daughter to be a virgin.
If there are witnesses that she was unfaithful while under him —
she has a marriage contract of one hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why רבא gave up the approach from the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That רבא's rule (nothing if he did not know) cannot stand
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of הוצאת שם רע, where she gets a מנה

steps.title: The ברייתא seems impossible: she should be stoned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how she can get a כתובה if witnesses saw her sin while she was bound to him. She would be put to death by סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are witnesses that she sinned while under him, she gets סקילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא, because it seems to make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who sins after אירוסין in front of witnesses gets סקילה. So it is strange to talk about her collecting a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to death by stoning

phrases.english: If there are witnesses that she was unfaithful while under him —
she is liable to stoning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line that she gets a מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sinning after אירוסין in front of witnesses means סקילה, not a כתובה.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means two cases. If she sinned after אירוסין, she gets סקילה. If she was with someone before, she gets a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: if there are witnesses that she sinned while under him, she gets סקילה. If she was with someone from before, she gets a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא by splitting it into two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this first reading, the מנה case is a woman who was with someone before אירוסין. The husband did not know that, yet she still gets a מנה. רב ששת builds a rule on this reading in the next step, but רבא will reject it in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
From the start; earlier, before אירוסין

steps.whatToRemember: On this first reading, a woman who was not a בתולה from before אירוסין gets a מנה, even though the husband did not know. רב ששת builds on this next, and רבא later replaces it with a different reading in step 23. That new reading is what leads to his retraction in step 25.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁזִּינְּתָה תַּחְתָּיו — בִּסְקִילָה.
phrases.english: If there are witnesses that she was unfaithful while under him — stoning.
If she was with someone from before —
she has a marriage contract of one hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the text as two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witnesses' case and the מנה are the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sinning after אירוסין means סקילה. Sinning before אירוסין means a מנה.

steps.title: רב ששת: a בעולה married as a בתולה gets a מנה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת learns from the ברייתא that if a man married a woman thinking she was a בתולה and she turned out to be a בעולה, she gets a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב ששת: This shows that if he married her as a presumed בתולה and she was found to be a בעולה, she gets a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת turns the ברייתא into a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though he married her thinking she was a בתולה, the marriage is not thrown out as a מקח טעות. She simply drops to the regular כתובה of a non-בתולה, which is a מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows; we learn from this
Presumed to be a בתולה
A woman who has already been with a man

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that being a בעולה lowers her כתובה but does not wipe it out. The next step challenges exactly that.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: And Rav Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav Sheshet said:
That is to say,
if he married her presumed to be a virgin
and she was found to be a non-virgin —
she has a marriage contract of one hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman married as a בתולה who turns out to be a בעולה gets a מנה.

steps.title: רב נחמן challenges רב ששת: here she gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings a משנה where the husband says she was not a בתולה before אירוסין and calls it a מקח טעות. There she gets nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objected: A man married a woman and found she was not a בתולה. She says, 'After you betrothed me I was forced, so it is his loss.' He says, 'No, it happened before I betrothed you, and my deal was a mistaken deal.' And she gets nothing at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב ששת's rule with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the husband's version, she was a בעולה before אירוסין. That is exactly רב ששת's case, yet the משנה treats it as a מקח טעות where she gets nothing. That clashes with רב ששת's rule that she gets a מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: I was forced
His field was flooded; it is his bad luck
A mistaken deal, which is void
She has nothing at all

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הָאִשָּׁה וְלֹא מָצָא לָהּ בְּתוּלִים,
phrases.english: One who marries a woman and did not find her to be a virgin,
she says: After you betrothed me I was forced
and his field was flooded.
phrases.notes: A saying that means the bad luck is his, since it happened after he was already bound to her.

phrases.english: And he says: Not so,
rather, it was before I betrothed you,
and my deal was a mistaken deal.
And she gets nothing at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's rule that a בעולה married as a בתולה gets a מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats a woman who was a בעולה before אירוסין as a מקח טעות with nothing at all, not a מנה.

steps.title: The great sages read 'מקח טעות' as losing only the 200
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין defends רב ששת. He says that רב עמרם and the great sages heard this teaching, felt this exact difficulty, and answered that 'מקח טעות' only takes away the 200. She still gets a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said: Is it possible that רב עמרם and all the great sages of the generation were sitting there when רב ששת said this teaching? They felt this difficulty and answered it: 'מקח טעות' only means she loses the two hundred. She still gets a מנה. And you say she gets nothing at all?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין answers רב נחמן's question from step 19. He says the great sages already dealt with it: the 'mistake' only takes away the 200, not the whole כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said 'מקח טעות' means she gets nothing, which goes against רב ששת. רב חייא בר אבין reads 'מקח טעות' more narrowly. The mistake was only about her being a בתולה, so she loses only the extra amount a בתולה gets, and her basic מנה stays.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or halachic ruling
The great sages of the generation
Two hundred זוז, the כתובה of a בתולה
One hundred זוז, the כתובה of a woman who is not a בתולה

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: And Rav Chiyya bar Avin said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר רַב עַמְרָם וְכׇל גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר
phrases.english: Is it possible that Rav Amram and all the great sages of the generation

phrases.aramaic: יָתְבִי כִּי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
phrases.english: were sitting there when Rav Sheshet said this teaching,
and it was difficult for them, and they answered:
What does 'mistaken transaction' mean here too? Only from the two hundred.
But she does have a maneh,
and you say she has nothing at all?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר רַב עַמְרָם וְכׇל גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's question from step 19 and defends רב ששת's ruling from step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מקח טעות' means she loses her whole כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מקח טעות' only takes away the 200. She still gets a מנה.

steps.title: רבא agrees with the objection: 'מקח טעות' means total
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב נחמן's question is a good one. 'מקח טעות' means the marriage is cancelled completely, so she gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The one who asks, asks well. 'מקח טעות' means totally.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against רב חייא בר אבין's answer. He sides with רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling something a 'mistaken transaction' means the whole deal was never valid. So the woman gets no כתובה at all, not even a מנה. This brings back the problem for רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a challenge (raises an objection)
Well, properly
Completely

phrases.english: And Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּקָא מוֹתֵיב — שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב:
phrases.english: The one who raises the objection raises the objection well:
'mistaken transaction' means completely.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּקָא מוֹתֵיב שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrow reading given in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'מקח טעות' only takes away the 200
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plain meaning of 'מקח טעות' is that the whole marriage is cancelled.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא about a מנה is difficult again
steps.stepSummary: If 'מקח טעות' means nothing at all, the גמרא asks about the ברייתא from step 15, which says she gets a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then that ברייתא is difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about רבא's view. It sets up the next step, where רבא will reread the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from steps 15-17 said a woman who was with someone before אירוסין gets a מנה. That clashes with רבא's claim that she gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (the earlier ברייתא)

phrases.english: But then that one is difficult?
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the ברייתא from step 15 about the husband's claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's view in step 21 using the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that 'מקח טעות' means nothing at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, as read in step 17, gives a מנה to a woman who was with someone before אירוסין.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא as three cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא rereads the ברייתא in three cases. If she sinned after אירוסין, she gets סקילה. If she was with someone before, she gets nothing. If she is a מוכת עץ, she gets a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fix it and say it like this: If there are witnesses that she sinned while bound to him, she gets stoning. If she was with someone from before, she gets nothing at all. If she turns out to be a מוכת עץ, she has a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by reading the ברייתא differently from step 17. The case that gets a מנה is now a מוכת עץ, not a woman who was with someone before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, 'was with someone before' got a מנה. Now that case gets nothing, which fits 'מקח טעות'. The מנה goes to a woman whose virginity was lost through an injury, since she never sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: Fix it, read it this way
A woman who lost her signs of virginity through an injury, not through relations
Death by stoning
From before (before אירוסין)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 17. There, a woman who was with someone before got a מנה. In רבא's new reading she gets nothing, and only a מוכת עץ gets a מנה.

phrases.english: Resolve it and say this:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁזִּינְּתָה תַּחְתָּיו — בִּסְקִילָה.
phrases.english: If there are witnesses that she sinned while bound to him, she gets stoning.
If she sinned from before, she gets nothing at all.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת מוּכַּת עֵץ יֵשׁ לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה מָנֶה.
phrases.english: If she turned out to be a mukat etz, she has a ketubah of a maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the cases in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מנה in the ברייתא goes to a woman who was with someone before אירוסין.
steps.terutzMaskana: That woman gets nothing. The מנה is for a מוכת עץ.

steps.title: רבא himself said a מוכת עץ gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבא himself ruled earlier that, according to the רבנן, a מוכת עץ gets nothing if the husband did not know. So how can he now give her a מנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it רבא who said that according to the רבנן, if he did not know about her, she gets nothing at all?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against רבא from his own earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the reading of step 23, a מוכת עץ gets a מנה even though the husband did not know about her. But earlier on the daf, רבא ruled that according to the רבנן, a מוכת עץ whom the husband did not know about gets nothing. The two statements contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Knew about her condition
The Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: But isn't it Rava who said, according to the Rabbis,
if he did not know about her, she gets nothing at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of step 23 using רבא's own earlier ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that a מוכת עץ gets a מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself ruled earlier that, according to the רבנן, an unknown מוכת עץ gets nothing.

steps.title: רבא took back his earlier ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבא retracted his earlier ruling about a מוכת עץ. Even if the husband did not know, she gets a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that רבא took back that earlier ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction: רבא changed his mind. This is the retraction mentioned back in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the ברייתא, רבא now holds that a מוכת עץ gets a מנה even if the husband did not know about her. His earlier ruling that she gets nothing no longer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, conclude from it
He took back his view

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture according to רבא: if she sinned after אירוסין, she gets סקילה. If she was with someone before אירוסין, it is a מקח טעות and she gets nothing. A מוכת עץ gets a מנה, even if the husband did not know.

phrases.english: Rather, conclude from this
that Rava retracted from that ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הֲדַר בֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵהַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא retracted. A מוכת עץ gets a מנה even if the husband did not know.

steps.title: After a first marriage, the second husband cannot claim she was not a בתולה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a first husband brought a woman into his home for marriage, a later husband cannot make a claim about her virginity. This is true even if witnesses say she was never secluded with the first husband long enough for relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If the first husband brought her in for marriage, and she has witnesses that she was not secluded with him, or that she was secluded but not long enough for relations, the second husband cannot make a טענת בתולים, because the first husband already brought her in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It is about when a second husband may claim his wife was not a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a woman has been brought into a husband's home for marriage, people assume she is no longer a בתולה. A second husband should have expected this, so he cannot claim he was fooled, even if witnesses say nothing happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Full marriage (after אירוסין)
She was secluded (alone with him)
Long enough for relations
A claim that she was not a בתולה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If the first husband brought her in for the purpose of marriage,
and she has witnesses that she was not secluded with him,
or alternatively, she was secluded,
but did not stay long enough for relations,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַשֵּׁנִי יָכוֹל לִטְעוֹן טַעֲנַת בְּתוּלִים.
phrases.english: the second husband cannot make a claim about virginity.
Since the first husband already brought her in.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּנָסָהּ רִאשׁוֹן לְשׁוּם נִישּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of רבא's view is settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a first husband brought her in for marriage, a second husband cannot make a claim about her virginity, even if witnesses say nothing happened.
